column4: 秦朝版图往南到今天的广东和广西省,往西南到今天的四川省。
column5: The territory of the Qin Dynasty went south to today's Guangdong and Guangxi provinces, and southwest to today's Sichuan Province.

column3: verb gradually (an uncontrollable change, often used with 变 or a verb + resultative)
column4: 用长城保护中国的想法也渐渐地变了。
column5: The idea of using the Great Wall to protect China has gradually changed.

column4: 在美国,每个州都有一个州府。在中国,每个省都有一个省会。
column5: In America, every state has a state capital. In China, every province has a provincial capital.

column1: 后来 vs. 以后 vs. 然后
column3: 后来 = later (past events only); 以后 = in the future (future events only); 然后 = and then (conjunction, often in 先 …… 然后 …… for sequence)
column4: 商周时代中国的版图很小。后来中国的版图经过了很多朝代,就越来越大了。
column5: China in the Shang and Zhou eras had a very small territory. Later, China's territory went through many dynasties, and it became bigger and bigger.

column3: is located in (place); frequently used in written language
column4: 四川省位于中国的西南部。
column5: Sichuan Province is located in the southwestern part of China.

column3: S is composed of (what follows 由 are the elements of the subject)
column4: 四川省由四川盆地和高原山地两大部分组成的。
column5: Sichuan Province is composed of two geographic parts, the Sichuan basin and the plateau.

column3: one of (noun/number); the number after 之 can be fluid, e.g. 三分之二 = 2/3
column4: 川菜是中国八大菜系之一。
column5: Sichuan food is one of the eight cuisines of Chinese food.

column3: . . . and so on (sometimes written as a single 等; often used at the end of a sentence)
column4: 有名的景点包括九寨沟、峨眉山等等。
column5: Famous scenic spots include Jiuzhaigou and Mt. Emei and so on.
